_why: Real defects this system shipped, each with the check that finds it now or a written statement that it cannot be checked. It exists to answer one question the gate cannot answer about itself: of the things that actually went wrong, how many would a person still have to notice by eye. ds-factory built the same ledger from this system's fix commits and measured 34 of 46 found by eye against 7 by the gate; this is the same instrument, kept here where the fixes land.
_seeded: SEEDED, NOT COMPLETE. docs/CHANGELOG-REVIEW.md carries 614 entries and only the ones below have been read and classified — every one states what was wrong in the words of the entry it came from, and nothing here is inferred from a heading. `unclassified` is the rest, and it is a number that falls as entries are read. A corpus that pretended to be complete would be the same lie as a check with the wrong population.

defects.was: the focus ring declared 56 times in 48 files, and ExpandButton — the one control in the button family that drew its own pill instead of composing Button — shipped with no :focus-visible rule at all, so the most visible floating action was invisible to a keyboard
defects.check: lint:rules · the focus ring is declared once
defects.evidence: gate-redteam breaks it and the step catches it; the recipes tier (2026-09-02) turned the ring into one value so a re-derivation is now also caught by lint:rules · a recipe is named, not rebuilt

defects.was: a fix from the day before wrapped everything containing `fr` in minmax(), so a column already declared minmax(11rem, 1fr) became minmax(8rem, minmax(11rem, 1fr)); a nested minmax is not a track, so the browser threw away the whole grid-template-columns and the catalogue collapsed into one column
defects.evidence: no static check reads a computed grid template: the value is legal CSS text and only the browser rejects it. The DOM-structure baselines (audit:pages) would catch the collapse on a screen that has such a grid, which is why the DataGrid example is in the gallery — but that is a baseline, not a rule, and it only holds the screens somebody shot.

defects.evidence: the check reported the pairs on its first run 2026-09-02, after jscpd had passed under its threshold on the same code

defects.check: lint:api · A1

defects.check: lint:rules · a recipe is named, not rebuilt

defects.was: check-skills resolved the repository root as three levels above its own file, which is the monorepo here and somebody else's directory in the published copy; in a scratch clone it walked the system temp directory looking for markdown and died on a macOS file it may not stat
defects.check: check:clone
defects.evidence: found on the first run of check:clone, 2026-09-02, in a check that had been green for months on this laptop

defects.was: axe keeps one global lock and the harness did not queue its runs; the suite passed here for months and failed in a scratch clone with a different core count, in a file nobody had changed. A test that passes because of how many cores you have is not a passing test
defects.check: check:clone
defects.evidence: found on the same first run; the canonical harness now queues axe and every app copy carries the fix (check:harness holds them byte-identical)

defects.was: two checks matched the ring by its ingredients, so the hour the recipe landed states-check called 32 of 34 controls ringless and lint:rules' restated-ring rule would have gone silent — a check that stops matching is worse than one that never existed, because it reads green over the hole

defects.evidence: states went red on the migration and named all 32; both checks now match the recipe and the ingredients

defects.was: a `git checkout --` of scripts/gates.mjs discarded an uncommitted step from an earlier session (gen:skill:check) along with the intended reset, and the gate went from 43 steps to 42 with nothing failing
defects.evidence: nothing can check that an uncommitted change was meant to survive. What made it recoverable was that the step list had been PRINTED earlier in the session, so the loss was visible by comparison; check:gates now fails a manifest that is internally inconsistent, but a step deleted cleanly leaves nothing to be inconsistent with.

defects.was: a product's bundle budget moved 242 to 248 in one afternoon with no code change, and read 243 an hour later, because its content directory was eager-globbed into the JavaScript every user downloads; the tripwire was measuring somebody's typing rather than our code
defects.check: size (in the product)
defects.evidence: Paid 2026-09-02, the same day it was written down. The content came out of the bundle the way that product's journal had in August: one endpoint serves it, a small store holds it, five screens read a hook instead of a field. Main chunk 249.3 -> 223.5 KB gzipped, and the budget was lowered 250 -> 224 rather than raised, so it measures our code again.

defects.was: the example stand was a grid whose track blockified whatever it held, so an inline-flex chip and a flex accordion arrived as identical boxes and the stand guessed the width for the component; an Accordion sat 328px wide inside a 711px panel
defects.check: audit:pages · width-used

defects.was: the same stand, from the other side: an atom example shrinks to max-content because a 40px button stretched across a panel is a control lost in a room, and a textarea asked the same question answered with one wrapped line and an empty half-panel
defects.check: audit:pages · width-used

defects.was: the list-detail panel grew 3:1 to a 26rem ceiling whatever was in it, and its group headings shared the size, weight and colour of the rows beneath them, so a label read as another row
defects.evidence: a heading that READS as a row is a judgement about type, not a fact about the DOM: the same markup with a heavier, tracked, smaller label is correct and nothing in the tree changed. What came out of it is a part (ListCluster's labelled run) so the treatment is decided once rather than judged again.

defects.was: a button inside an Alert looked disabled: --surface-contrast answered 'what does a quiet element fill itself with' for two cases — grey page means white, white card means grey — and an Alert declaring itself a card was a third surface neither case knew about
defects.check: boundary
defects.evidence: boundary walks every surface a control can land on rather than a list of two, which is the population lesson one check earlier than the token one

defects.was: the owner opened the gallery and named four cards in a row — a chat bubble filled --muted on a --muted stand, an overview example with nothing in its prime zone, inline code that was a styled span, an agents page claiming a count nobody had counted — and not one of the four was caught by the gate, because each was green by its own rule and wrong on the screen
defects.check: audit:pages, check:claims
defects.evidence: the entry is the ratio in miniature and is why the structure baselines and the claims check exist; two of the four are now rules (a surface on the same surface, a countable claim), and the other two were content

defects.was: the page header is sticky and opaque so content scrolls under it, which is right, and its bottom edge sat exactly on the top of the first field: the focus ring is drawn OUTSIDE the box, so the top of it was painted over by the header
defects.evidence: nothing static can see it: the markup is correct, the ring is correct, and the overlap exists only after the cascade, at one scroll position, at one width. The structure baselines would catch the geometry changing, not the geometry being wrong the first time.

defects.was: five columns forced into 390px turned NAME into NAM and SAR 3,663 into 63, while the Table beside it had always done the right thing through TableScroll: a sheet the reader swipes is readable, a sheet squeezed to fit is not, whatever it fits into
defects.check: audit:pages · no-overflow
defects.evidence: and the first fix failed, which is recorded with it: a width floor plus scrolling on the body fixed the reading and broke the header alignment

defects.was: two halves of one mechanism with nothing between them: NavDrawerButton asks a SidebarProvider to open the drawer and renders nothing at all without one, while AppLayout moved its rail from its own navOpen prop. An app that mounted the shell without thinking about the provider got a phone with no way into the navigation
defects.check: audit:pages · nav-reachable
defects.evidence: the page audit has a nav-reachable rule per width since, and the mechanism is one thing rather than two halves

defects.was: the sign-in example declared autoComplete='email', so the browser filled the owner's real address into a screenshot fixture — and the same screen had no brand mark, a product name set in the body face on the one screen a reader reaches before they are sure they are in the right place
defects.check: scan:secrets
defects.evidence: the secret scan reads what git carries, which is where a filled-in address would have landed; the autocomplete itself is now off in the fixtures

defects.was: AGENTS.md promises that a fresh clone of the published repository installs and passes every step of its gate by itself; checked after a publish, the proof was red — gen:data:check failed on facts.json and specs.json because the clone counted zero specs where the published data said seventeen, since the specs of real products are on the drop list and the count was not
defects.check: check:clone
defects.evidence: the check that performs that proof exists now and runs the CI gate inside the clone, rather than a person remembering to try it after a publish

defects.was: a tab crashed with Cannot read properties of undefined because one store held two shapes: meetings booked from the cockpit carry a slot, meetings linked by pasting somebody elses invitation do not, and the type declared start and end as required — so TypeScript called the read safe. It crashed on one team only, the one with two linked meetings, and it crashed with the modal CLOSED, because JSX children are evaluated before the dialog decides to render nothing
defects.check: typecheck
defects.evidence: the type describes what is actually in the file now, with the optional fields optional and a flag for the linked kind, so the next such read does not compile. The check existed and was lied to; what changed is the truth it reads.

defects.was: a full-page template stood on a white card in the gallery with a grey strip above it, because it was missing from surfaces.json and both the generator and the gallery silently default to card. The cosmetic half was the small half: the wrong context went into the REGISTRY, so an agent reading it learned that a full-page template lives inside a card
defects.check: lint:rules · every component and block has a surface context
defects.evidence: the rule walked src/components only and blocks had never been in it — three of seven had no context. It walks both now, and catches the reverse case too, an entry with no folder.

defects.was: sixty test files, zero tests executed: jsdom 30 moved localStorage and sessionStorage from own properties of window onto Window.prototype, and vitest builds its global from a fixed list plus getOwnPropertyNames — neither name is in the list and it does not walk the prototype, so both arrived undefined. The error named neither jsdom nor vitest and read like a broken provider
defects.check: test:cov
defects.evidence: the suite itself was the check that caught it, loudly and unhelpfully. The shim is a module rather than lines in the setup because setup.ts imports i18n first and imports run before the body of the file — the fix was one import too late until the order was made visible.

defects.was: <Icon> accepted only name, size and className and dropped everything else, and TypeScript deliberately does not check hyphenated JSX attributes — so Rating's per-star `data-fill` was accepted by the types and lost at runtime. `.rating-star[data-fill='full']` matched nothing and EVERY star drew as an outline: four out of five looked exactly like zero. The rule against reaching into a primitive's class+data contract was already written beside it (owner, 2026-08-24); the defect came back invisible because the screenshot had been accepted with it
defects.check: mutate · a mutant that used to die may not start surviving
defects.evidence: found while writing a test to kill the `fill >= 0` mutant: the assertion came back null instead of 'empty' because the attribute was not in the DOM at all. Neither a person looking at the gallery nor any gate step had noticed

defects.was: NumberInput's Props extended Omit<InputHTMLAttributes, ...> without omitting `size`, and InputHTMLAttributes carries its own `size?: number` — the ancient HTML width-in-characters attribute. The intersection of number with 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' is a type nothing can be assigned to, so the prop could not be passed at all, while the registry published it as a working axis and an agent following the contract got a type error
defects.check: lint:rules · a redeclared DOM prop is omitted first
defects.evidence: tsc cannot say it: an impossible prop nobody passes is not an error until somebody writes the call. The rule keys off the BASE TYPE rather than a list of suspicious words — `size` clashes on input and select and is free on a span — and was verified both ways. lint:api A5 would now also catch it: a prop nobody can pass is a prop nobody passes

defects.was: a card separates itself by FILL, not by outline: on the page's muted ground white is the separation, and on white it is not. The outline for that case was written one container at a time — `.card .card` here, `.detail-page[data-panels] .card` there — so a container nobody had written the rule for got white on white. The showcase's own component stage was exactly such a container: three cards in the Layout example read as bare headings in one large white box
defects.check: boundary · SC 1.4.11, a control edge against every surface it can land on
defects.evidence: the fix was structural — `[data-surface="card"]` declares the surface once instead of a growing list of special cases — and `boundary` walks every control edge against every surface a part can land on, which is the same question one level down. What it does NOT cover is a CARD on an unexpected surface: that is still the visual baselines of the screens somebody shot, and it is why the Layout example is one of them

defects.was: NavDrawerButton — which PageHeader puts on every screen without a back arrow — asks SidebarProvider to open the drawer and renders nothing at all when there is no provider, while AppLayout moved the rail from its own `navOpen` prop. Two halves of one mechanism with nothing between them: an app that mounted the shell without thinking about the provider gave a phone no way to reach navigation, which is the exact failure NavDrawerButton was written to prevent. This system's own site was such an app
defects.evidence: the owner said "the menu does not open in responsive" and it was true. No static check reads whether a context provider is mounted above a component that needs one; the fix was to make the shell own the drawer so no app has to remember

defects.was: the AppLayout golden example disagreed with the shell this system's own site runs on in three places: a bare glyph in `logo` and a different one in `logoMark` instead of one BrandMark in both, nav items that were not links (so middle click, copy address and the back button did nothing), and a rail that never said it collapses
defects.evidence: checked against apps/showcase/src/site/SiteShell.tsx rather than written from memory. Nothing compares an example to a real screen: the example compiles, renders and is axe-clean while teaching a composition nobody uses

defects.was: a mutation run cut short — a piped `head`, a Ctrl-C — left both the mutation and its backup file in the source tree, and the backup then shipped as a component file
defects.check: mutate · the runner sweeps on exit
defects.evidence: the same sweep-on-exit pattern was given to gate-redteam when it landed, for the same reason: a tool that edits the tree must restore it however it ends

defects.was: the owner reported four legibility failures by looking at screens, with every static check green: a card title over a photograph as dark ink on a dark scrim, a Chip on the page surface in the exact colour of the page, an icon button turning its glyph brand-blue on hover alone in its family, and a row title recolouring on hover where a card title underlines. Three of the four are CASCADE bugs — a descendant setting its own colour inside a surface that had inverted its ink — which no reading of semantic.css can see; the fourth sat on a gradient, which has no single colour to compare against at all
defects.check: ink · every run of text measured against the median colour of its own box
defects.evidence: `npm run ink` measures pixels instead of tokens: two frames from one DOM, the second with every glyph made transparent, so the ground can be a token, a gradient, a photograph or three nested surfaces. It found 14 more the moment it ran, and joined the gate on 2026-09-03 after five of its own measurement bugs were found and fixed

defects.was: the first run of `npm run ink` reported a wall of exactly-1.00 failures: `__show()` sets React state and the theme attribute follows on the next commit, so computed colours were read in the PREVIOUS theme while the frame already carried the new one
defects.evidence: a measurement bug in a new check, caught by its own implausible output — 1.00 contrast everywhere is not a design defect. Nothing checks a check's own timing; what stands in for it is that a check reporting a colour nobody painted is worse than no check, because somebody goes and changes the colour

defects.was: 33 controls answered hover, press, focus, disabled and invalid 31 different ways: a checkbox did not acknowledge the pointer at all, Checkbox / Radio / Switch / FileUpload had no `invalid` (so a required consent box could be rejected with nothing on screen saying which box), ChatComposer, Tag and SearchInput had no focus ring, ContextMenu had no aria-activedescendant, and `ghost` and `quiet` drew one button between them
defects.check: states · one control, one set of answers
defects.evidence: the check asks each question only where it means something — a control you type into answers a click with focus rather than a press, a breadcrumb has no disabled state, a component wearing another's class inherits its answers. Getting those three wrong first produced 31 findings of which 8 were noise, which is the reason the population rule exists

defects.was: `npm run ink` took its ground frame immediately after inserting the stylesheet that makes every glyph transparent. Inserting a stylesheet resolves as soon as the node is in the head; the paint happens on a later frame, so the "ground" still had the text in it for whichever cases lost the race. Ink then equalled ground and the ratio came out at 1.0-1.1: three consecutive runs of an unchanged tree reported 18, 21 and 25 findings, all in that band
defects.evidence: found by running the same check three times and diffing the output — a check whose findings shuffle is not measuring the thing it names. Nothing checks a check for determinism except check:determinism, which reads the spec engine and not a browser. After the two-frame wait, three consecutive runs gave the same six findings

defects.was: SessionPill's action link painted `--primary`, which is a SURFACE colour and stays brand-400 in the dark theme, so "Back to the board" measured 2.08:1 as ink on the pill's own card. Every other piece of text that goes somewhere uses `--link`, which moves to brand-200 in dark
defects.check: ink · every run of text measured against the median colour of its own box
defects.evidence: npm run contrast reads the pairs the tokens declare and this pair was never declared: a component reached past the roles and took the fill colour for ink. That is the case ink exists for, and it is the first defect the check found on its own rather than the day it was written

defects.was: the DiffTable's "before" column paints `--muted-foreground` to read as quiet, and that class also lands on the cells carrying the removed TONE. Muted grey on the dark removed tint measures 4.39:1 — the toned cell already carried --destructive-soft-foreground, and the quiet class beat it
defects.check: ink · every run of text measured against the median colour of its own box
defects.evidence: exactly the shape the check was written for after 2026-08-23: a descendant setting its own colour inside a surface that had inverted its ink, which no reading of the tokens can see. Fixed by scoping the quiet colour to cells with no tone

defects.was: `npm run ink` injected its glyph-hiding stylesheet with addStyleTag and then tagged "whatever is last in the head" so it could remove it again. Whatever is last in the head is not reliably the sheet just added — Vite and React both put styles there — and when the tag missed, the sheet stayed applied for every case after it: their text was transparent in BOTH frames, so no pixels changed, so every run of text in them was skipped. The check reported 824 runs of text where there are 1757
defects.check: ink · the sheet is one element addressed by id
defects.evidence: found by asking why a case that should have failed did not, and the number in the header answered it. A check that measures half of what it names is the quietest way to be wrong, and nothing in the gate reads another check's coverage — this is the argument for printing the population in the header of every check that has one

defects.was: ink read the computed colour with a regex for `rgb(...)`. A colour authored with `color-mix(in oklch, …)` comes back as `oklch(0.889606 0.00240303 none)`, so every element wearing one was skipped rather than measured — silently. The gate red team's own break was invisible for exactly this reason
defects.check: gate-redteam · contrast: ink that is legal in the tokens and unreadable on the screen
defects.evidence: the break was written, the gate went red, and the step that should have caught it said nothing. The page now converts every colour through a 1x1 canvas, which is the browser answering in sRGB whatever the notation

defects.was: the static scorer excused a component the agent had imported — "imported from their own app, so it is theirs" — without looking at WHERE from. `@ds/DataTable` is the system's own namespace, and an unknown name there is exactly an invented one. The first class of failure the whole harness exists to catch, reached by the most natural thing an agent does
defects.check: mcp/server.test.mjs · the exception depends on the source
defects.evidence: found by a hard audit whose method was to break the repository once per category and see who noticed, rather than to read the checks. The guard is a test rather than a red-team mutation on purpose: the hole was in the wrapper, and a mutation there would have depicted coverage that did not exist

defects.was: a made-up prop name went uncaught on 27 of 143 registry entries — Button, Card, Badge, Alert, Avatar, Checkbox, the ones every screen uses. Parts marked `inherits` skipped the check entirely, on the grounds that a component spreading `...rest` accepts DOM attributes. It does — but `padding="huge"` is not a DOM attribute, and React itself complains about it
defects.check: evals/scorers.mjs · checked against the list of real attributes
defects.evidence: the same audit. The list of real attributes grows from a loud report rather than from silently skipping a whole component, which is the shape the original exemption had

defects.was: a card family losing its specimen was a WARNING: the gate printed "30/31" in grey and exited 0. That was right while the specimens were being written and stopped being right the moment the 31st landed
defects.check: check:spec · a family without a specimen fails
defects.evidence: coverage that only counts is not a check. It is the line that opens gate-redteam, because it is the cheapest way for a check to be green and mean nothing

defects.was: SectionLabel published an EMPTY prop list while owning the `as` that decides whether it is a heading or a div. Its type was written as an intersection in the signature, and both fallback readers in the registry generator were blind to that shape — so the one prop that decides the heading outline was invisible to every agent reading the registry
defects.check: gen-registry:check · a main export that parses its parameters and publishes zero props is an error
defects.evidence: found by a live agent run losing 12 points on heading-order, which is the eval harness catching a registry defect through a screen rather than through the registry

defects.was: a wrong finding was being reverted with `git checkout`, and the file it restored had unsaved work in it: Table.tsx went from 310 lines to 99. Restored from the vendored copy taken the same day and compared byte for byte against the registry generated before the loss
defects.evidence: nothing can check an editor's unsaved buffer. What it argues for is the vendored copies, which exist for a different reason and were the thing that made this recoverable — and for reverting by writing the previous content rather than by discarding the working tree

defects.was: `iconEnd` was read by no line of CSS, and the golden example of Button demonstrated it — and after it EmptyState, PageHeader, Table, ListPageTemplate and 24 more files. A prop that does nothing, taught in 59 places by the examples an agent copies from
defects.check: lint:api A5 · every published prop is passed somewhere in this package
defects.evidence: stripped from the 28 files that autumn and finally deleted from the API on 2026-09-03, when A5 counted it among the 78 props nothing in the package passes. The check that would have caught it on the day it went inert did not exist for another seven days

defects.was: the rule "does this part have a golden example" answered yes for all 131 and asked nothing further. `<Button>Save</Button>` is not an example of Button, it is a photograph of one: the reader learns the component exists and nothing about the decision it carries. 76 of 131 examples were that
defects.check: lint:rules · an example shows two values of a union prop the registry publishes
defects.evidence: the axis is derived from the contract rather than from a list: a part with no union — Spinner, Divider — is exempt by construction. The 76 are recorded as WORK, and the list only shrinks: a name comes off by rewriting the example, never by being added back

defects.was: lint:mechanisms counted apps/showcase as a place a mechanism could have its caller. The showcase exists in the monorepo and not in the published package, so the same code passed here and failed in a clone — ErrorBoundary, which five products mount at their route boundary and nothing inside a library can
defects.check: check:clone · a fresh clone installs from its lockfile and passes the CI gate
defects.evidence: the second defect of this exact shape that check:clone has found (the first was a script resolving the repository root three levels above its own file). The population is now the package alone, which is the thing the published copy IS, and a mechanism whose only caller is a product writes `published because …` — which is what that escape hatch was for

defects.was: a semantic token pointing at another semantic token is the one place in the layer where editing one role silently moves another, and nothing checked it. `--link-hover` followed `--primary-hover` in light and NOT in dark — where a hover cannot go deeper, only lighter — and `--nav-active-foreground` wrote `var(--brand-200)` by hand in dark: the same value `--primary-accent` already had, arrived at separately, and it would have fallen behind the day the brand moved
defects.check: lint:token-vocab · every alias is declared with the role it follows and the reason
defects.evidence: all 11 aliases are declared; an undeclared one, one declared against the wrong role, and one declared for something the CSS no longer has all fail. `diverges` names the theme in which an alias deliberately does not hold, which is what makes the light/dark pair sayable at all

defects.was: the workshops prompt snapshot guarded two different things at once. Its job is that templating did not change what the model is asked; but `{{designSystem}}` resolves through a LIVE read of the registry, so every new part rewrote six prompts. It was regenerated by hand five times in one day
defects.check: apps/workshops server unit tests · the SHAPE of the block is checked, not its contents
defects.evidence: a check that shouts on an ordinary day is a check people learn to regenerate without reading. The block is cut from the snapshot (100 KB → 22 KB) and its shape is asserted separately — the menu is there, the catalogue is not empty, the lines are readable. Proven both ways: a new component fails nothing, a template edit fails only the snapshot, an empty registry fails only the shape check

defects.was: a batch request said `pending` for six weeks after two of its three parts shipped, and the check written against exactly that — "pending while the part is in the registry" — passed, because the request was NAMED "Code, Prose, ColorSwatch" and no file in the registry has that name
defects.check: check:requests · every name in a batch is checked on its own
defects.evidence: a partially built batch is the loudest case, not the quietest: it is the one where the folder is wrong about what has already happened. The check now splits the name

defects.was: the raw-controls rule read the SENTENCE about `<input type="color">` in ColorSwatch's own documentation — the sentence explaining that this component replaces it — as a violation. The same hole was in six more rules: any file naming the markup it forbids was punished for explaining itself
defects.check: lint:rules · all seven read through a comment strip
defects.evidence: line numbers are preserved through the strip, and the rules were re-proven to bite on real code. The cost of the alternative is in the same entry: a part the contract hides costs more than it saves, because an agent that cannot see ColorSwatch reaches for the raw input

defects.was: the overview tile's glyph became 24 where it had been 20, inside the same disc: 0.33% of pixels against a 0.5% tolerance, so the photograph passed
defects.evidence: caught by looking at the pair of shots rather than at the green tick. The DOM-structure baseline catches a changed ATTRIBUTE and this was a changed size inside one; the tolerance exists because type rasterises differently per OS, and lowering it to catch this would make every clone red. It is the case the owner's rule covers: a green gate is not evidence a screen looks right

defects.was: 82.6% statement coverage said which lines RAN and nothing about whether anyone would notice them breaking. The first mutation run answered it: 207 mutants, 120 killed, 58% — a third of the breakages would have gone unseen, and the worst operators were `invert-comparison` (21 survivors), `and-to-or` (17) and `off-by-one` (11), which is boundary logic
defects.check: mutate · a mutant that used to die may not start surviving
defects.evidence: the score is a floor now (80% today) and mutate:check holds it. Five accessible names had nothing holding them — the slider, the page number, the card group, the filter field, the save failure in a grid — and each new test was verified by KILLING its mutant rather than by being green

defects.was: Slider took its accessible name from both a visible `<label for>` and an `aria-label`: two names for one control, identical right up to the day somebody edits one of them, and then people HEAR the one they cannot see (WCAG 2.5.3)
defects.check: mutate · two mutants that turned out to be twins
defects.evidence: found because two mutants died to the same assertion. The aria-label is gone — the visible label IS the name. DataGrid's `title` + `aria-label` pair with one string was kept deliberately: a title is the mouse hint, and there is nowhere for the two to diverge

defects.was: measured rather than assumed: the same model, the same three tasks, working in an empty folder with no AGENTS.md, no registry and no src/ scored 61% against 100% with the system — and wrote 499, 674 and 298 lines where the reference solutions are 79, 63 and 80. Six times the code and 39 points worse, failing in exactly the ways the system names: raw <button> and <table>, borrowed `card` and `badge` class names, missing required props
defects.check: eval · scores a candidate solution against the system
defects.evidence: this is the number the whole package exists to move, and it is measured on every eval run rather than argued about. It is also why lint:api A5 matters: a prop an agent reads and nobody has rendered is context spent on something that may not work

defects.was: AGENTS.md — the file every agent reads in every session — said "the icon goes on the left by default, pass `iconEnd` for add/create". The owner reversed that convention on 2026-06-10: `.btn > .icon` has carried `order: 1` ever since, the icon always trails, and no line of CSS reads `data-icon-end`. The prop was dead, the CSS comment said so, and the contract taught it for three months
defects.check: lint:api A5 · every published prop is passed somewhere in this package
defects.evidence: check:claims holds the COUNTABLE claims in the contract and a reversed rule is prose, so nothing would have caught the sentence. What closed it for good is the prop: A5 found `iconEnd` among the 78 nothing in the package passes, it was deleted on 2026-09-03, and the sentence has nothing left to be wrong about. The durable fix for a contract that teaches a dead prop is to delete the prop

defects.was: not one of 782 props published its own description to the registry. The field splitter cut on a newline, JSDoc is multi-line, and every comment was torn off its prop and thrown away. An agent saw the name, the type and the allowed values; WHY a prop exists and when NOT to pass it reached nobody
defects.check: gen-registry:check · every prop carrying a decision publishes what it decides
defects.evidence: the registry IS the interface for an agent, and this was the half of it that says what to do. Found while reading what the generator actually emitted rather than trusting that it emitted it

defects.was: the full mutation run takes 14 minutes — twenty times the whole gate — and a step that costs that is a step somebody deletes
defects.check: mutate:check · only the parts whose code or test moved since the last measure
defects.evidence: 0.2 seconds when nothing moved. And it fails on the right thing: not a falling score, but a mutant that USED to die and started surviving — a test that stopped biting

_unclassifiedMeans: Entries in docs/CHANGELOG-REVIEW.md that nobody has read into this corpus yet. 609 entries, five read. It falls by reading, never by rounding.
_sample: The entries read so far are not a random sample and the ratio should be read knowing it: they cluster in the weeks when the gate was already mature, which flatters it. The three from 11-13 August are a deliberate step back into a thinner period, and two of the three were still found by a person opening a screen. The 2026-08-23 entries added on 2026-09-03 are a second such step: that day alone carried four legibility failures found by eye with every check green, and the check that answers them (ink) was written the same afternoon.
